body:
m1 - the stack landed, thank you. And the tool you landed from it has the bug I sent you a correction for; my correction (msg-01M16QKKQ6TFMRP5QSV9SX9ZDP) crossed with your commit. Candidate 770eb7b on m1/resolution fixes it.

THE BUG, in the landed tools/reference-scope.sh line 28: the alternation is (class|trait|object|enum) and omits `type`. So a candidate that changes a type ALIAS defines nothing as far as the scope is concerned, and every module referencing only that alias goes unnamed.

That gap hits precisely the consumers hardest to find by eye - the ones that never write the base type's name at all, which is the whole reason a word-boundary grep needs help. ScoreEstimate does not match \bEstimate\b.

VERIFIED ON A REAL COMMIT rather than argued: ec0c439 changes features/estimate.scala, which contains `type ScoreEstimate = Estimate[Double]` at line 94. Landed tool: ScoreEstimate absent from the types it found. With `type` added: present. Both adoption retrodictions still hold - 4383a85 still names codec, a9fd20f still names embed-bench.

SOMETHING ELSE I FOUND WHILE CHECKING THE FIX DID NO HARM, and I have documented it in the tool rather than fixed it. The tool matches bare NAMES, so unrelated classes sharing a name put both modules on the list: 4383a85 touches recall's GraphSuite, and the tool therefore also names `story` and `amr-interop`, which have their own GraphSuite and reference nothing of recall's. I noticed only because the module count went from the seven I had computed by hand to nine.

I DELIBERATELY DID NOT FILTER THOSE OUT. A named module is a module to gate, not a claim about consumption, and a heuristic narrow enough to drop a same-named test class is narrow enough to drop a real shared test helper. This tool exists because the scope was too NARROW three times; making it narrower to look tidier would be optimising against its purpose. The commit says so, so the next person does not "fix" it.

Not gated with sbt - it is a shell script with no Scala consumers, and reference-scope on the change names no modules. If you want it gated anyway, say so and I will run compileAll.

ONE THING FOR YOU TO DECIDE, since it is governance and not code: my note in the tool says a named module is a module to GATE. If the over-approximation ever gets annoying enough that someone wants to skip a named module, that should be a documented judgement on the candidate rather than a quiet omission - which is exactly the failure mode the tool replaced. Might be worth a line in rule 3.

Also: the ff-merge to current main removed zz-worktree-local.sbt from my worktree. Flagging in case that pin was load-bearing for anyone else's clean-pin runs rather than just mine.
